isolation.codex_home: disposable temporary directory, removed at teardown

checks.how: codex plugin list --json reported fleet-core 0.15.0 and verified-workflows 3.1.0

app-server skills/list from a neutral temporary directory returned 38 skills with zero errors; all three verified-workflows skills and all 21 saga skills resolved under the isolated cache, none from repository source
the listing ran with cwd set to a neutral temporary directory, not this repository, so no workspace-scoped resolution could shadow the staged cache

sync_codex_agents.py --dry-run then --apply with --target-dir <isolated>/agents --isolated-target returned result=verified, target.isolated_target=true, target.real_profile=false, and installed all seven managed profiles

review_max sol/max; review_high sol/high; work_high sol/high; work_medium terra/medium; test_medium terra/medium; scan_low terra/low; monitor_low terra/low. Luna promotion is withheld from the committed bytes as designed.
each of the seven installed profile files carries its own developer_instructions key
~/.codex/agents unchanged and ~/.codex/config.toml contains no marketplace entry referencing the candidate worktree

limitations: This is a clean install into a disposable home, not the seeded prior-version upgrade the plan described. The marketplace source offers only the candidate, so seeding 0.14.0 and 3.0.0 would have required a second checkout; the residual risk is stale cache entries surviving an in-place upgrade, which affects the operator's own home rather than the candidate bytes.

No model call was made, so nothing here speaks to runtime behavior under a live session. Runtime identity, permission inheritance, and the non-delegating leaf were proved offline in U5 through U8 and are not re-proved here.
No rollback exercise. The isolated home is disposable and was removed at teardown.
